Understanding Initial Approval

Initial approval is a critical step in the business setup process. It indicates that your application has met the requirements set by the relevant authorities. This approval confirms that your business activity complies with local regulations. It allows you to move forward with obtaining the necessary permits and licenses.

It is essential to understand this stage. As it sets the foundation for your business operations. Additionally, it ensures that you are on the right track to successfully establish your venture.

Steps to Check Initial Approval Status Online

All set to start your business, but have you checked the initial approval status online? If not, we are going to share the steps here to check the initial approval status online.

Visit the Relevant Authority’s Website:

Navigate to the official website of the licensing authority or free zone governing your business.

Access the Online Portal:

Look for the section dedicated to business services or application tracking. Many authorities have a dedicated portal for checking application statuses.

Enter Required Information:

Input the necessary details, such as your application number, business name, or identification information, as prompted.

Submit the Request:

After entering the required information, click on the submit or search button to retrieve your approval status.

Review the Status:

The portal will display your initial approval status, along with any additional details or next steps you may need to take.

Contact Support if Needed:

Consider reaching out to the support or customer service team of the authority for assistance. In case you encounter any issues or need further clarification.

If you’re performing a DED initial approval status check for a mainland business in Dubai, visit the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) website at https://www.investindubai.gov.ae/.

How Long Does Initial Approval Take?

Timelines vary by jurisdiction and business activity:

  • Free zones: Often issued digitally within hours to a couple of business days for straightforward activities, since most free zones now run fully online application systems.
  • Mainland (DED/DET): Generally 3 to 7 business days for standard activities. This can extend if your activity requires external approvals from another regulator (health, transport, telecom, etc.), in which case it may take longer depending on that authority’s own processing time.

These are typical ranges, not guarantees — processing speed can shift with demand and how complete your documentation is on submission.

 

Tips for Checking Initial Approval Status

Worried about how to check initial approval status? Then, this blog part is a perfect fit. Here, we go through the tips that help you check the initial approval status. Let’s go and find out what those tricks are for a smooth process.

  • Confirm your jurisdiction before you start. Know whether your application is with DED/DET (mainland) or a specific free zone authority. Checking the wrong portal is the single most common reason people think their application “isn’t showing up.”
  • Have your reference number ready, not just your business name. Status portals match faster and more reliably on the application/transaction number issued at submission than on a business name search, especially if your trade name isn’t finalized yet.
  • Use UAE Pass where available. Many government and free zone portals now support UAE Pass login, which is faster and reduces the chance of being locked out of your own application.
  • Check your registered email and phone, not just the portal. Authorities frequently send status updates or document requests directly, and a missed message is a common cause of unexplained delays.
  • Know the difference between “pending” and “rejected.” A pending status usually just means processing is ongoing. A rejection will typically state a reason, most often a naming conflict, an activity restricted to UAE/GCC nationals, or incomplete documentation, and will require resubmission rather than just waiting.
  • Don’t let your approval lapse. Since initial approval (mainland) is generally valid for six months, track that window so you don’t have to restart the process if you’re delayed in completing tenancy or licensing steps.
  • Save a copy of your initial approval certificate as soon as it’s issued. You’ll need it for tenancy contracts, external approvals, and the license application itself.

FAQs:

What is an initial approval in the UAE business setup process?

Initial approval is the government’s confirmation that your business activity is permitted and you can proceed with setup procedures.

How can I check my initial approval status in Dubai?

Visit the Dubai Economy (DED) website, enter your application number, and view your current initial approval status online.

How long does it take to receive initial approval in the UAE?

Typically, free zone approvals are being issued in the same day to 48 hours digitally, with mainland sometimes still in that 3-7 day range when external approvals are needed.

How long is the initial approval valid in Dubai?

Mainland initial approval is generally valid for six months, giving you time to complete tenancy, documentation, and licensing before it expires.

Is it possible to check the initial approval status through a PRO service?

Yes. KPM PRO can track your approval status directly with authorities, ensuring accurate updates and faster communication.

What does it mean if my initial approval status shows as rejected?

A rejection usually comes with a stated reason, commonly a trade name conflict, an activity restricted to UAE or GCC nationals, or missing documentation. You’ll need to address the issue and resubmit rather than simply wait for the status to change.

Is initial approval different for free zone companies?

Yes. Free zone companies apply for and check initial approval through their own free zone authority’s portal, not through DED/DET. The two systems don’t share status information, so always check with the authority you actually applied through.

Can I amend my initial approval after it’s issued?

Yes. If your activity, partners, or legal form changes after initial approval is issued, DED/DET and most free zone authorities offer an amendment service, processed separately and usually for an additional fee.
